topic: AWS Certified AI Practitioner (AIF-C01) certification exam preparation
exam_format: 65 questions (50 scored + 15 unscored), 90 minutes, passing score 700/1000
question_types: multiple choice, multiple response, ordering, matching, case study
audience: Cloud practitioners, developers, analysts, and business professionals who want to prove foundational AI/ML knowledge on AWS. No ML experience required; ~6 months of AWS familiarity helpful.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Domain 1: Fundamentals of AI and ML
domains.notes: AI/ML/DL definitions, types of learning, ML lifecycle, AWS AI services (SageMaker, Comprehend, Rekognition, Transcribe, Polly, Translate, Lex, Personalize)

domains.name: Domain 2: Fundamentals of Generative AI
domains.notes: Foundation models, tokens, embeddings, prompt basics, transformer concept, use cases, GenAI lifecycle, Amazon Bedrock, PartyRock, Amazon Q

domains.name: Domain 3: Applications of Foundation Models
domains.notes: Prompt engineering techniques, inference parameters (temperature, top-p, top-k), RAG, vector databases (OpenSearch, Aurora pgvector), fine-tuning vs continued pre-training, Bedrock Agents, Knowledge Bases, Guardrails, model evaluation (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore)

domains.name: Domain 4: Guidelines for Responsible AI
domains.notes: Bias, fairness, explainability, SageMaker Clarify, Model Cards, Bedrock Guardrails, human-centered design, dataset balance, legal risks (hallucination, IP)

domains.name: Domain 5: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
domains.notes: IAM, encryption (KMS), Macie, PrivateLink, VPC endpoints, shared responsibility, AWS Artifact, Audit Manager, CloudTrail, data lineage, governance frameworks

extra_guidance: Emphasize Bedrock heavily (most-tested service). Include exact inference parameter effects, pricing model comparisons (on-demand vs provisioned throughput), and RAG vs fine-tuning decision rules. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation walkthrough with strategy.
